text: Telegram, also known as Telegram Messenger, is a cloud-based, cross-platform social media and instant messaging service that launched for iOS on 14 August 2013 and for Android on 20 October 2013. It enables users to exchange messages, share media and files, and conduct private and group voice or video calls, as well as public livestreams. Available on Android, iOS, Windows, macOS, Linux, and web browsers, Telegram offers end-to-end encryption in voice and video calls and optionally in private chats if both participants use a mobile device. The service includes social networking features such as posting stories, creating public groups with up to 200,000 members, and sharing one-way updates to unlimited audiences via channels. Founded in 2013 by Pavel and Nikolai Durov, Telegram previously had its roots in the Russian social network VK, which the brothers left in 2014, citing government control. Nikolai developed the MTProto protocol, the foundation of the messenger, while Pavel provided financial support through his Digital Fortress fund. Telegram is registered as a company in the British Virgin Islands and as an LLC in Dubai, with its headquarters in Dubai, United Arab Emirates. Its servers are distributed worldwide through a complex network of shell companies to avoid compliance with government subpoenas, and the company claims it does not process requests related to illegal content in chats or group chats, stating it has disclosed zero bytes of user messages to third parties, including governments. However, Pavel reported that Telegram disclosed data for 203 legal requests from Brazil and 6,992 from India between January and September 2024. Users can check their country's legal requests via Telegram’s transparency bot. As of March 2025, Telegram has more than 1 billion monthly active users, with India being the country with the most users. The app reached 100,000 daily active users in October 2013, 35 million monthly users and 15 million daily active users by March 2014, 50 million active users and 1 billion daily messages by December 2014, 60 million active users and 12 billion daily messages in September 2015, 100 million monthly active users and 15 billion daily messages in February 2016, 180 million in December 2017, 200 million by March 2018, 300 million monthly active users by October 2019, 400 million in April 2020, 500 million in January 2021, 700 million in June 2022, 800 million in July 2023, 900 million in March 2024, 950 million in July 2024, and surpassed 1 billion monthly active users in March 2025. Registration requires either a phone number and a smartphone or one of a limited number of non-fungible tokens (NFTs) issued in 2022. Users must sign up on an Android or iOS device, and changing a phone number automatically reassigns the account without notifying contacts or exporting data. Messages are tied to the user’s number and custom username, not the device, and are synced across logged-in devices via cloud storage, except for device-specific secret chats. Inactive accounts are deleted after six months, with a range of up to 18 months. Groups and channels can be verified if they have a verified social media or Wikipedia page, but individual user accounts cannot. Messages support formatted text, media, files up to 2 GB (4 GB with Premium), locations, and audio or video messages; private chat messages can be edited for up to 48 hours with an "edited" icon, and messages or entire chats can be deleted without a trace. Chat history can be imported from WhatsApp, Line, and KakaoTalk. Users can start a message on one device and finish it on another via cloud drafts. Messages can be translated, with Premium users able to translate entire chats with one click and hide the translate button for specific languages. Reactions with emoji are available in private chats and can be enabled by admins in groups and channels, with Premium users having more options and the ability to leave multiple reactions. Stickers, including static, animated, or video types, are supported and use WebP or WebM formats, with full-screen effects possible. Messages can be scheduled to send at a specific time or when a conversation partner comes online, or sent without sound. Private chat messages can be forwarded with the original sender hidden or captions hidden, and forwarded messages retain reply formatting. A "Saved Messages" chat allows users to bookmark messages, visible only to themselves. Chats can be sorted into folders with preset or custom categories, and Premium users can set any folder as the default screen. Secret Chats are end-to-end encrypted, accessible only on the device where they started, and self-destruct upon logout; they restrict screenshots on Android and warn on iOS, hide content from screenshots, and support perfect forward secrecy with key rotation after 100 uses or weekly. Secret Chats are available on Android, iOS, and macOS. Messages in both secret and regular chats can self-destruct after being read, with a user-set duration from one day to one year. Groups support up to 200,000 members and can be public or private, with flexible admin rights and bots for moderation. Groups can be split into topics, and admins can hide member lists or post anonymously. Content protection prevents screenshots, forwarding, and downloading of media. Ownership of groups and channels can be transferred to an admin. Groups support threaded replies and tagging users with @username. Polls can be open or anonymous with multiple choices, and votes retain when forwarded. Channels are one-way feeds where owners or admins post content, and followers can only read, react, and comment if enabled. Channels can reach unlimited subscribers and show detailed statistics only to admins. Channel owners can run giveaways to award prizes like Telegram Premium subscriptions. Premium users can give "boosts" to channels, unlocking features such as custom messages or posting stories. In December 2019, Bloomberg News moved its newsletter from WhatsApp to Telegram after WhatsApp banned bulk messaging. Other news organizations with official channels include the Financial Times, Business Insider, and The New York Times. Channels have been used by governments and heads of state, such as Volodymyr Zelenskyy and Emmanuel Macron, and by journalists in oppressive regimes to create independent news networks. Telegram offers an open API for third-party bots, many built on the 8XR game engine, with Mini Apps reaching 500 million monthly active users in July 2024. Since 2017, users have been able to initiate one-on-one calls; video calls were introduced in August 2020, and a neural network is used to improve call quality. Group voice chats were launched in December 2020 and group video chats in June 2021, supporting picture-in-picture, screen sharing, recording, noise suppression, and selective muting. Channels support livestreams that integrate with third-party apps like OBS Studio and XSplit. Group voice chats remain open until an admin closes them. In April 2025, Telegram launched secure group calls with end-to-end encryption using blockchain-like technology, supporting up to 200 participants with voice, video, and screen sharing. Login requires either an SMS or a code from another active session, with two-step verification and recovery email options added in late 2022, and support for Sign in with Apple, Google, or email. A login alert is sent when a new device logs in. Users can hide their "Last Seen" status, phone number, and profile photo, with Premium users able to restrict who can send them text or voice messages. The Devices submenu shows active devices and allows remote logout. Media autoplay and automatic downloads can be disabled for WiFi and mobile data, with settings adjustable by chat type. Cache can be cleared when it reaches a certain size or time, with visual storage usage and media sorting by size available. In June 2015, Telegram launched a bot platform allowing third-party developers to create bots that respond to messages, integrate services, or host mini apps. Bots can accept payments via Paymentwall and Yandex.Money. Inline bots can be accessed from any chat screen by typing a username and query, and certain approved bots integrate into the attachment menu. A Dutch report noted that an invited bot can potentially read all group messages if access is changed silently, and Telegram indicated it would announce such changes in the group.

In June 2015, Telegram launched a platform enabling third-party developers to create bots, which are Telegram accounts operated by programs capable of responding to messages or mentions, being invited into groups, performing tasks, integrating with other programs, and hosting mini apps. These bots can accept online payments via Paymentwall, Yandex.Money, Stripe, Ravepay, Razorpay, QiWi, and Google Pay, depending on the country. Bots power Telegram’s gaming platform using HTML5, with games loading on-demand and compatible with iPhone 4 and newer, and Android 4.4 and newer devices. Through IFTTT, users can interact with Internet of Things (IoT) services. In April 2021, the Payments 2.0 upgrade allowed bot payments in any chat using third-party services such as Sberbank, Tranzoo, Payme, CLICK, LiqPay, and ECOMMPAY to process credit card information. Bots are widely used by businesses to communicate with customers via APIs integrated with communication platforms, enabling omnichannel inbox functionality, website chat widgets, and automated or human-assisted conversations; platforms like respond.io, Manychat, and Trengo offer such integrations. In February 2018, Telegram introduced Telegram Login, a website widget allowing users to sign into third-party sites with their Telegram account, sharing only their name, username, and profile picture while keeping their phone number hidden, with the gateway linked to a bot tied to the developer’s domain. In June 2021, a new bot menu was introduced, allowing users to browse and send commands during chats. In April 2022, bots gained support for customized interfaces and inline page loading, with interfaces adjustable to match the app’s theme even during interactions. In October 2024, Telegram increased messaging limits for bots to 1000 messages per second, with messages beyond the free 30-per-second limit charged using Telegram Stars. In December 2024, Telegram introduced affiliate programs enabling developers to create programs where users earn commissions for referring others to bots or mini apps. Telegram has over 40,000 stickers, which are cloud-based, high-resolution images used to provide expressive emoji, organized into collections called "packs," with one default pack included; stickers are automatically available across all clients and use the WebP format, with animated emoji introduced in August 2019, interactive emoji added in September 2021, and video stickers in January 2022 using the WebM format. In August 2022, users could upload custom emoji via Telegram’s emoji platform, though only Premium users can use them in chats. Reactions were introduced in 2021 and expanded in September 2022 to include dozens of options for free users, with the reaction panel redesigned. Features People Nearby and Groups Near Me, which used GPS to connect users nearby, were removed in 2024 due to issues with bots and scammers. Telegram users can post stories with dual-camera mode, privacy settings, post-editing, and rewind/fast-forward capabilities. Telegram Premium, launched on 19 June 2022 with regional pricing, offers increased limits such as larger file uploads, faster downloads, unlimited voice message transcription, more pinned chats and folders, extra stickers, emoji, reactions, customization features like a special badge, and message appearance changes, as well as instant chat translation and restrictions on who can send text or voice messages. Premium can be purchased via Apple and Google in-app purchases, through Telegram’s @PremiumBot, or with cryptocurrency on the Fragment platform, and can be bought for oneself or as a gift, or won through official Channel Giveaways. In October 2024, Telegram launched Gifts, virtual cosmetic items purchasable and sendable using Telegram Stars, and in January 2025, Collectible Gifts were introduced—unique collections with special artwork and attributes, some of which can be upgraded to unlock random appearances and other features, registered on the TON blockchain as NFTs and tradeable on Telegram’s in-app Gift Marketplace or external platforms. In July 2025, Telegram partnered with Snoop Dogg to release limited-edition collectible gifts with his music video "Gifts," and in November 2025, partnered with Khabib Nurmagomedov and UFC for two limited-edition releases using an auction-based system. Users can publish articles on Telegraph, a minimalistic text editor and publisher, with anonymous publishing and the ability to check view counts and edit content later; articles support Instant View, allowing full reading in chats without opening a browser. The URL is auto-generated from the title, with non-Latin characters transliterated, spaces replaced by hyphens, and the publication date appended, e.g., /Telegraph-blog-platform-11-17 for an article titled "Telegraph (blog platform)" published on 17 November. Text formatting includes two levels of headings, single-level lists, bold, italics, quotes, hyperlinks, image and video uploads (limited to 5 MB, disabled since September 2024), and direct embedding of YouTube, Vimeo, or Twitter links. In July 2018, Telegram introduced Telegram Passport, a real-life identification system allowing users to upload official documents like passports or driver’s licenses, with data shared only with authorized recipients and no access by Telegram; however, the service was criticized for vulnerability to brute-force attacks. In December 2020, Telegram launched a Bugs and Suggestions platform where users submit bug reports and feature ideas, which others can vote on and comment. In October 2024, Telegram introduced a verification platform, Telegram Gateway, enabling third-party services to authenticate users via verification codes sent through Telegram. For encrypted chats (Secret Chats), Telegram uses MTProto, a custom symmetric encryption scheme developed by Nikolai Durov and other developers, based on 256-bit AES, 2048-bit RSA, and Diffie–Hellman key exchange; MTProto 1.0 was deprecated in December 2017 in favor of MTProto 2.0, deployed starting with version 4.6, which was formally proven correct in December 2020 by a team from the University of Udine, Italy, using ProVerif, confirming its security properties including authentication, integrity, confidentiality, and perfect forward secrecy, though the team noted that the server is not trusted and man-in-the-middle attacks are possible if users fail to verify shared key fingerprints, and that full computational model proofs are needed for definitive security. Telegram uses centralized servers in multiple countries, with closed-source, proprietary server-side software; Pavel Durov stated that connecting independent servers would require a major architectural redesign. For users in the European Economic Area (EEA) or UK, GDPR is supported by storing data only in the Netherlands and designating a London-based company as responsible data controller. Telegram offers various client apps, many free and open-source under the GNU GPL version 2 or 3, with official clients supporting all file formats and media types including JPEG, PNG, WebP, H.264, HEVC, MP4, and MP3, FLAC, Vorbis, Opus, AAC; clients are available for non-traditional platforms like KaiOS (Telekram) and S30+/Mocor feature phones. In 2021, Telegram announced a direct build of its Android app, available directly from the Telegram website, automatically updated and faster than versions in app stores, with a unique feature allowing access to channels/groups on specific topics without censorship due to app store policies. The iOS version was written in Swift, the Android version uses TDLib, and the iOS version was discontinued with its code merged into the main app. Telegram provides public APIs for developers to build instant messaging apps, and in February 2015, the creators of WhatsApp+ released Telegram Plus, later renamed Plus Messenger, after receiving a cease-and-desist from WhatsApp; Samsung released a messaging app based on these APIs in September 2015. Telegram also offers a bot API for developers to create bots, used for emulating old games and informing users about vaccine availability during the COVID-19 pandemic. In addition, Telegram enables direct payments within the platform using external services like Stripe. In 2025, Telegram’s founder claimed that xAI signed a $300 million program with Telegram for Grok to provide full functions within Telegram starting in Summer 2025, funded by a mix of cash and xAI equity, though the initiative has since been abandoned with no new announcements or feature releases. Initially supported by Pavel Durov’s personal funds after selling his VK stake, Telegram conducted a private placement in January 2018, raising $1.7 billion from investors including Kleiner Perkins, Sequoia Capital, and Benchmark; after the TON project shutdown, the company had to repay investors for funds not spent on development. On 15 March 2021, Telegram issued a $1 billion five-year public bonds placement to cover $625.7 million in debts, including $433 million from investors who bought Gram token futures, such as David Yakobashvili; on 23 March, it sold an additional $150 million to Mubadala Investment Company and Abu Dhabi Catalyst Partners. The next day, Mubadala stated that Russia’s sovereign wealth fund participated in the deal through a joint UAE-Russia investment platform, though Telegram denied RDIF was among investors, confirming that the funds involved did not include RDIF. Bondholders have the option to convert bonds to shares at a 10% discount if Telegram conducts an open IPO. Durov stated the bond move aimed to enable global growth while maintaining independence and values, having previously rejected offers for a 5–10% stake, valuing the company at $30–40 billion. In March 2024, Telegram sold an additional $330 million in bonds, with Durov stating it would further solidify Telegram’s position as an independent platform challenging industry 'Goliaths'. Telegram has stated it will never serve advertisements in private chats; in late 2020, Durov announced work on an internal ad platform to integrate non-targeted advertising.

Durov stated that Telegram’s bond issuance aimed to "enable Telegram to continue growing globally while sticking to its values and remaining independent." Prior to the bond placement, Durov had rejected investment offers for a 5–10% stake in the company, valuing it between $30–40 billion, and in March 2024, Telegram sold an additional $330 million in bonds. Durov said the bond sale "will further solidify our position as an independent platform that is able to challenge the 'Goliaths' of our industry." According to the bond contract, holders will be given the option to convert their bonds into shares at a 10% discount if the company conducts an open IPO. Telegram has stated it will never serve advertisements in private chats, but began offering non-targeted ads in public one-to-many channels through its "Sponsored Messages" platform in October 2021, starting with channels having more than 1,000 followers. In late 2020, Durov announced Telegram would consider adding paid enterprise features requiring more bandwidth, with costs covered by feature prices and partially offsetting regular user costs. In June 2024, Telegram launched Telegram Stars to facilitate in-app purchases of digital goods and services, in compliance with App Store and Play Store policies, and later expanded functionality to allow Stars to unlock media in channels or buy gifts for other users. In December 2024, Telegram CEO Pavel Durov announced the company had reached profitability due to significant growth in Premium subscriptions and ad sales, supported by other monetization features launched in 2024. In 2017, Telegram began developing a blockchain platform called "The Open Network" (TON) and its native cryptocurrency "Gram," announced in mid-December 2017 and with a 132-page technical paper released in January 2018. The codebase was developed by Pavel Durov’s brother Nikolai Durov, the core developer of Telegram’s MTProto protocol. In January and February 2018, Telegram conducted a private sale of Gram futures, raising around $1.7 billion, with no public offering. The TON development was isolated and delayed, with a test network launched in January 2019 and the main network scheduled for 31 October 2019. On 30 October, the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission obtained a temporary restraining order to block Gram distribution to initial purchasers, considering the offering an unregistered securities transaction. Judge P. Kevin Castel agreed with the SEC, maintaining the ban, which applied to non-U.S.-based purchasers due to Telegram’s inability to prevent resale to U.S. citizens on secondary markets, given user anonymity. Durov announced the end of Telegram’s active involvement with TON, and on 26 June, the judge approved a settlement where Telegram paid an $18.5 million penalty and returned $1.22 billion to Gram purchasers. In March 2021, Telegram launched a bonds offering to cover the debt and fund further growth. The TON ecosystem was later developed by others and began offering decentralized domain names and cloud storage via TON DNS. Telegram’s mixed nature—combining private communication with social media features and minimal content restrictions—has led to its use by organizations for recruitment and spreading agendas, including in Belarus, Russia, Hong Kong, and Iran, as well as for state propaganda and extremist views. Research institutions and monitoring bodies have criticized Telegram for being used by violent groups like ISIS, the Proud Boys, and the Myanmar junta for private and public communication. Telegram has made efforts to ban illegal content, including child abuse and pro-terrorist channels, including a partnership with Europol to eliminate IS presence, though far-right extremist communities remain active. Durov argued that removing conspiracy theories strengthens them, as their content is removed. In September 2024, Telegram announced it would hand over users’ IP addresses and phone numbers to authorities with valid legal requests. Martin Jäger, head of Germany’s BND, warned Russia was recruiting saboteurs across Europe via Telegram by monitoring pro-Russian channels. A study by OpenMinds, published before the 2025 Moldovan parliamentary election, found a third of Telegram channels in Moldova systematically spread Russian propaganda and one in eight comments came from bots; Moldovan President Maia Sandu criticized Telegram for refusing to collaborate with state authorities on illegal activities like vote buying. In September 2015, Durov stated privacy was more important than fear of terrorism and sarcastically suggested banning words used by terrorists. ISIS used Telegram for recruitment, and in France, initial investigations of a terrorist act revealed Telegram use, though the extent was unclear. Telegram began publishing daily moderation statistics on terror-related content in an official channel named @ISISwatch, and after removing such content, ISIS reportedly moved its recruitment groups to the dark web, with U.S. officials citing the deplatforming as effective. In 2023, Saudi Arabia’s Etidal reported over 59 million pieces of extremist content were removed from Telegram since 2022. The Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps used Telegram to dox citizens and share propaganda in 2020, and after the 2021 Myanmar coup, the junta used the platform to spread propaganda and organize misinformation campaigns, prompting Telegram to ban 13 accounts linked to the military. On 26 April 2023, Telegram was temporarily suspended in Brazil and fined R$1 million per day for failing to comply with a Federal Police investigation into neo-Nazi activities; the company only partially fulfilled a data request, which authorities deemed intentional lack of cooperation, and the suspension was lifted three days later but the fine remained. Telegram’s CEO claimed the requested data was technologically impossible to obtain. Twelve days later, Telegram warned users that Brazil’s upcoming Congressional Bill No. 2630 would end freedom of speech. Far-right and white supremacist groups on Telegram have shared videos of the Christchurch and Halle shootings after they were removed from Twitch. British far-right publication TR.news launched a Telegram channel after multiple deplatformings, and the Institute for Strategic Dialogue reported Irish far-right groups grew substantially between 2019 and 2020. Oxford University research suggests Telegram’s lack of sorting algorithms keeps many extremist groups obscure while some gain attention. Telegram has been used to distribute illegal pornography, including child pornography, and has a reporting system for child abuse content, including specific messages, with a verified channel "Stop Child Abuse" posting daily statistics on banned groups and channels and an email for abuse reports. In January 2021, a banned Telegram group called "Public Room" ("Јавна соба") with over 7,000 members shared nude photos of women and teenage girls, including their private information like phone numbers and social media profiles, encouraging contact for sexual favors without consent, causing public backlash and demands from North Macedonian leaders for action; the group was banned without a public statement. In August 2024, a BBC investigation found Telegram had not joined the U.S. National Center for Missing & Exploited Children or the UK Internet Watch Foundation, and Telegram responded that it proactively moderates harmful content within industry standards. In August 2024, journalist Ko Narin exposed Telegram chats where teenagers used generative AI to deepfake images of classmates and teachers for porn. In May 2020, Volodymyr Flents of "Electronic Democracy" reported a Telegram bot selling personal data of Ukrainian citizens, estimated to contain data from 26 million Ukrainians in the Diia app; deputy prime minister Mykhailo Fedorov denied data leaks, and 25 people were confirmed as involved with 30 databases seized. In 2020, Apple blocked a Telegram bot for posting deepfake pornography, and Telegram reportedly banned over 350,000 bots and channels containing child abuse and terrorism-related content. In 2021, a bot was found selling leaked Facebook phone numbers. Telegram has faced criticism for fraud, primarily involving scammers offering online jobs with "prepaid tasks" that entice users to deposit money with false promises of returns. In July 2023, Hyderabad Police uncovered a fraud where 15,000 Indian citizens lost ₹712 crore (US$84 million) in less than a year through such tasks, originating in China and laundered via cryptocurrency wallets. In September 2023, Singapore Police reported over 6,600 Singaporeans lost S$96.8 million (US$72.24 million) to prepaid job scams on Telegram and WhatsApp. In March 2024, a Spanish judge ordered the temporary blocking of Telegram in Spain following complaints from media organizations about unauthorized sharing of copyrighted content; the order was suspended pending a police report and later annulled as "disproportionate." In recent years, Telegram has become popular for illicit drug trading, with a 2024 paper by Sociology Compass exploring this trend. In August 2024, an EU probe was launched to determine if Telegram breached EU digital rules by failing to provide accurate user numbers. Telegram stated in February 2024 it had 41 million users in the EU, but under the EU Digital Services Act, it was required to provide an updated number by August 2024 and only declared it had "significantly fewer than 45 million average monthly active recipients in the EU." As part of its monetization model, Telegram displays advertisement banners in public channels with over 1,000 subscribers, with revenue shared with channel owners in Toncoin cryptocurrency; as of August 2025, there was no opt-out option, which is seen as problematic for non-profit organizations. In August 2025, Germany’s public broadcaster NDR closed its tagesschau Telegram channel after editorial staff discovered unsolicited advertisements, which they argued violated the Rundfunkstaatsvertrag, especially "shady" or "fraudulent" sports betting ads; NDR stated the accumulation of Toncoin from unsolicited ads was unacceptable. In 2025, Telegram blocked Huione Guarantee, an escrow-style marketplace operating across thousands of Telegram channels and widely used by online scammers based in Cambodia, with Hun To, cousin of Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, listed as a director. Channels have been used by celebrities such as Arnold Schwarzenegger and Snoop Dogg, and politicians including President Emmanuel Macron of France, former President Jair Bolsonaro of Brazil, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President Maia Sandu of Moldova, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy of Ukraine, former President Andrés Manuel López Obrador of Mexico, and former Singaporean Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong.

Not noticed these ads before, but closed the channel, stating that an advertisement-based accumulation of Toncoin, albeit unsolicited and not withdrawn, was unacceptable for a German public media broadcaster. In 2025, Telegram said it blocked Huione Guarantee, which Elliptic described as an escrow-style marketplace operating across thousands of Telegram channels and widely used by online scammers based in scam centers in Cambodia; Huione lists businessman Hun To, cousin of Cambodian Prime Minister Hun Manet, as a director. Channels have been used by celebrities such as Arnold Schwarzenegger and Snoop Dogg and politicians: President of France Emmanuel Macron, former President of Brazil Jair Bolsonaro, Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdoğan, President of Moldova Maia Sandu, President of Ukraine Volodymyr Zelenskyy, former Mexican President Andrés Manuel López Obrador, former Singaporean Prime Minister Lee Hsien Loong, President of Uzbekistan Shavkat Mirziyoyev, former Taiwan President Tsai Ing-wen, Ethiopian Prime Minister Abiy Ahmed, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, and others. Telegram's security model has received notable criticism by cryptography experts, who criticized how, unless modified first, the default general security model stores all contacts, messages and media together with their decryption keys on its servers continuously, and that it does not enable end-to-end encryption for messages by default; Pavel Durov has argued that this is because it helps to avoid third-party unsecured backups and to allow users to access messages and files from any device. Criticisms were also aimed at Telegram's use of a custom-designed encryption protocol. In December 2020, a study titled "Automated Symbolic Verification of Telegram's MTProto 2.0" was published, confirming the security of the updated MTProto 2.0 and reviewing it while pointing out several theoretical vulnerabilities; the paper provides "fully automated proof of the soundness of MTProto 2.0's authentication, normal chat, end-to-end encrypted chat, and re-keying mechanisms with respect to several security properties, including authentication, integrity, confidentiality and perfect forward secrecy" and "proves the formal correctness of MTProto 2.0", partially addressing concerns about lack of scrutiny while confirming the formal security of the protocol's latest version. The desktop clients, excluding the macOS client, do not feature options for end-to-end encrypted messages; when the user assigns a local password in the desktop application, data is also locally encrypted. Telegram has defended the lack of ubiquitous end-to-end encryption by saying that online-backups that do not use client-side encryption are "the most secure solution currently possible". Telegram has organized two cryptography contests to challenge its own security; third parties were asked to break the service's cryptography and disclose the information contained within a secret chat between two computer-controlled users, with rewards of US$200,000 and US$300,000 offered; both contests expired with no winners. Security researcher Moxie Marlinspike, founder of the competing Signal messenger, and commenters on Hacker News criticized the first contest for being rigged or framed in Telegram's favor and said that Telegram's statements on the value of these contests as proof of the cryptography's quality are misleading, because the cryptography contest could not be won even with completely broken algorithms such as MD2 (hash function) used as key stream extractor, and primitives such as the Dual EC DRBG that is known to be backdoored. Telegram has been blocked temporarily or permanently by some governments including Iran, China, Brazil, and Pakistan; the Russian government blocked Telegram for several years before lifting the ban in 2020. The company's founder has said he wants the app to have an anti-censorship tool for Iran and China similar to the app's role in fighting censorship in Russia. On 19 April 2024, Apple removed Telegram from the App Store in China. In September 2024, Ukraine banned the usage of Telegram by government officials, military personnel, and key workers on official devices, citing fears of Russian espionage; the National Security and Defense Council of Ukraine enforced the restrictions following evidence reported to them by Kyrylo Budanov, showing Russia's ability to access messages and user data on the platform; Andriy Kovalenko, head of the security council's centre on countering disinformation, clarified that the ban was limited to official devices and did not extend to personal phones. Telegram was the main subject surrounding the 2019 Puerto Rico riots that ended up in the resignation of then-Governor Ricardo Rosselló; hundreds of pages of a group chat between Rosselló and members of his staff were leaked, with the messages considered vulgar, racist, and homophobic, and members of the chat discussing how they would use the media to target potential political opponents. In September 2021, prior to the regional elections in Russia, Telegram suspended several bots spreading information about the election, including a bot run by the opposition party and critics of incumbent president Vladimir Putin's government, citing election silence as the reason, though a blog post by the company's CEO implied the company was following Apple and Google, which "dictate the rules of the game to developers"; the blocking of the main Smart Voting bot was criticized by allies of Alexei Navalny, a Kremlin critic and former opposition leader; Navalny's spokeswoman Kira Yarmysh called the block and the deletion of the tactical voting app from app stores "censorship [...] imposed by private companies". In a later blog post, Durov directly stated that the block was a result of pressure from Google and Apple as refusal to comply with their policies would result "in an immediate shutdown of Telegram for millions of users"; the post included a screenshot showing an internal email sent by the App Store to developers, demanding the takedown of content related to Navalny. On 24 November 2022, Telegram disclosed the admin names, phone numbers and IP addresses of channels accused of unauthorised sharing of national exam study materials following an order by the Delhi High Court which rejected Telegram's argument that its regional servers were located in Singapore and thus no data could be disclosed as the local laws prohibit it. On 24 August 2024, Pavel Durov, who is both a French and UAE citizen, was arrested in France by French authorities; on 28 August he was charged with a wide array of crimes, including complicity in managing an online platform to enable illegal transactions; complicity in crimes such as enabling the distribution of child sexual abuse material; drug trafficking and fraud; and refusal to cooperate with law enforcement authorities; Durov posted bail of five million Euros, was barred from leaving France, and was released on condition he report to a French police station twice weekly; the case would be handled by a special magistrate with investigative and prosecutorial powers.
